name: Jose Joao Abdalla Filho
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Jose Joao Abdalla Filho is the son of J. J. Abdalla, a Brazilian entrepreneur and politician who built a real estate and textile company.
In the 1950s, the group his father led became one the largest manufacturers of cement in the country, employing over 40,000 people.
Abdalla Filho used the money he inherited to open Banco Classico, which owns stakes in a number of Brazilian companies.
His Banco Classico owns 5% of Eletrobras, Brazil's largest electric utility, and almost 7% of Cemig, an energy giant that owns over 200 companies.
forbes_facts: His late father J.J. Abdalla was a doctor, businessman, and politician. He became mayor of Birigui, a small town in the state of Sao Paulo, and a congressman.
A vast amount of land owned by the Abdallas in a central neighborhood in S?o Paulo was expropriated by the government in 1988.

name: Ranjan Pai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2020)
forbes_bio: Medical doctor Ranjan Pai is chairman of the Manipal Group, an education and healthcare empire with 7 universities and 29 hospitals.
The Manipal Group was started in 1953 by his grandfather T.M.A Pai, who founded India's first privately-owned medical school in the town of Manipal in  Karnataka.
Singapore fund Temasek increased its stake in Manipal Hospitals to 59% in 2023 after acquiring shares from Pai and other investors, valuing the chain at $4.6 billion. Pai retains a 30% stake.
Pai's Manipal Global Education Services has expanded overseas with campuses in Malaysia, Antigua, Dubai and Nepal. His other assets include Manipal Cigna Health Insurance.
He is the largest shareholder in test prep outfit Akash Educational Service  after he increased his stake to more than 50% in November 2025.
forbes_facts: Pai also owns Bangalore-based Stempeutics, which develops stem cell products using adult stem cells.
In January 2023, he invested $2 million in Kites Senior Care, which provides home-based care and dementia care.

name: Roberto Hartono
forbes_bio: Roberto Hartono is the president commissioner of Hartono Istana Teknologi.  He inherited his wealth from his late father Michael "Bambang" Hartono.
Michael was among the richest in Indonesia and owned a stake in Bank Central Asia together with his brother R. Budi. Michael died in March 2026 at age 86.
The Hartonos bought the stake in BCA after another wealthy family, the Salims, lost control of the bank during the 1997-1998 Asian economic crisis.
The family first got rich in tobacco and is still one of the biggest clove cigarette makers in the nation.

Family holdings also include prime real estate in Jakarta and popular electronics brand Polytron, which forayed into the EV business on its home turf in 2025 with the launch of two electric car models.
forbes_facts: In what was Indonesia's second-largest IPO of 2022, the Hartonos listed Global Digital Niaga, which owns e-commerce giant Blibli, raising $510 million.

name: Cui Genliang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2020); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Cui Genliang chairs Hengtong Group, the main investor in Shanghai-listed Hengtong Optic-electric, a maker of optical fiber and optical cables.
Cui's other business interests include real estate and financial investments.
Before joining the company, he was a factory worker for both garment and rubber.

name: Howard Marks
sec_insider_companies: STARTENGINE CROWDFUNDING, INC. (STGC) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Howard Marks is the cofounder and co-chairman of Oaktree Capital Management, a Los Angeles-based distressed debt investor with over $220 billion in assets.
Marks began his career at Citibank, where he started a portfolio of high-yield bonds after meeting with junk bond king Michael Milken.
He became an asset manager at TCW, where he met Oaktree cofounder Bruce Karsh. The duo left with four colleagues in 1995 to found their own shop.
In September 2019, Brookfield Asset Management acquired 61% of Oaktree for about $4.9 billion in cash and stock.  It agreed to buy the rest for $3 billion in 2025.
He and Karsh still head up Oaktree, which continues to operate independently of Brookfield. His stake in the firm is now about 7.5%.
forbes_facts: Marks is known for his highly detailed investment memos, which cover everything from cryptocurrency to index investing.
The Wharton and UChicago alum minored in Japanese studies, which he became interested in after signing up for a mandatory literature class.

name: John Liew
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2020); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: John Liew cofounded AQR, a quantitative investment manager with $187 billion in assets under management.
AQR stands for Applied Quantitative Research. It invests based on quantitative and proprietary signals, offering products including hedge funds, mutual funds and separately managed accounts.
Before cofounding AQR, Liew worked at Goldman Sachs as a portfolio manager, where he developed and managed quantitative trading strategies.
The firm is headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut, with other locations in Bangaluru, Dubai, Hong Kong, London, Munich and Sydney.
forbes_facts: Liew is a member of the University of Chicago?s Board of Trustees, his alma mater, and sits on the university's investment committee.
He earned a B.A. in economics, an M.B.A. and a Ph.D. in finance all from the University of Chicago.

name: Thomas Mueller
forbes_bio: Raised in rural Idaho, Mueller joined SpaceX in 2002 as employee No. 1, with a master's in mechanical engineering and experience building experimental rockets.
He and Elon Musk outlined plans for SpaceX's first rocket, Falcon 1, shortly after Musk sold PayPal to eBay, laying the foundation for the company's launch vehicle program.
As head of propulsion engineering, Mueller led the design and development of rocket engines for the Falcon launch vehicles and the Dragon spacecraft.
He departed SpaceX in 2020 to found Impulse Space, an aerospace startup focused on in-space transportation and orbital logistics.
Impulse has signed contracts with satellite provider SES, SpaceX, and NASA.

name: Kokuei Yuan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Kokuei Yuan is a director of Hong Kong-based crypto exchange Bullish.
Bullish was founded in 2020 and went public on the New York Stock Exchange in August 2025.
Yuan owns a 25% stake in the company. Bullish cofounder Brendan Blumer owns 28% and is also a billionaire.
Yuan previously served as executive chairman of block.one, a digital asset investment firm that Blumer cofounded in 2016. Bullish was majority-owned by block.one until 2024.
Yuan, who studied economics and studio art at Tufts University, worked as an investment banker earlier in his career.
